record_schema.schema: atlas.sandbox-run.v2 (core::sandbox::SANDBOX_RUN_SCHEMA); v1 records (atlas.sandbox-run.v1) still read: every added field is optional; none is committed under .atlas/evidence

request_fields_added.confinement: Option<Confinement{toolchain: Vec<ToolchainPath{path}>, proc: bool}>: Some selects the confined class (backend atlas.sandbox.confined-subprocess.v1); None the restricted-subprocess class (atlas.sandbox.restricted-subprocess.v1)
request_fields_added.toolchain_binaries: Vec<String>: absolute paths of further binaries to identify (in the confined class each under a declared toolchain path)
request_fields_added.pinned_toolchain: Option<ToolchainIdentity>: the identity the run must have

run_fields_added.toolchain: Option<ToolchainIdentity{program: BinaryIdentity, binaries: Vec<BinaryIdentity> (sorted by path), version: Option<String> (`-vV` stdout for rustc/cargo)}>; BinaryIdentity{path (as found), resolved (links resolved), digest (BLAKE3-256 of the resolved file, the declared-input digest function)}
run_fields_added.refusal_kind: Option<RefusalKind>: REQUEST_MALFORMED, INPUT_ESCAPES, INPUT_UNREADABLE, INPUT_DIGEST_MISMATCH, OUTPUT_ESCAPES, PROGRAM_NOT_ON_PATH, ENVIRONMENT_REFUSED, TOOLCHAIN_PATH_REFUSED, PROGRAM_OUTSIDE_TOOLCHAIN, TOOLCHAIN_PROXY, TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_ABSENT, TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, CONFINEMENT_UNAVAILABLE

record_schema.request_identity: canonical_request appends confinement, toolchain_binaries and pinned_toolchain lines only when present, each value length-prefixed (`<bytes>:<value>`): a request without them keeps its v1 digest (core test pins the v1 text). Injectivity, on the requests that pass core::sandbox::request_defect, up to the order of inputs, outputs, toolchain paths and toolchain_binaries (the canonical form sorts them; their order does not change what runs: inputs staged by path, outputs digested by path, toolchain paths bound and binaries identified sorted; the record lists outputs in request order, so consumers compare outputs as a set, by path): request_defect refuses (REQUEST_MALFORMED, before anything runs) a control character in the program, an argument, a single empty argument (args [""] joined like args [] -- review round 3), an input/output path, an environment name or value, a toolchain path or binary; `=` or emptiness in an environment name; an input digest that is not blake3-256:<64 hex> (so the input line ends unambiguously); and a program path that is not a bare name or a normalized absolute path. A malformed request is identified by BLAKE3 of "atlas.sandbox-request.malformed\n" + its JSON, a tag no canonical text starts with (review finding f3).

mechanism.outer: unshare --user --map-root-user --mount --pid --fork --kill-child --propagation private [--net] -- sh -c CONFINE_SCRIPT (constant; values only as positional parameters; helpers run with an empty environment from /)
root_layout: / : private tmpfs, remounted read-only, nosuid,nodev, mode 0755
/work : the stage (digest-verified input copies), read-write, nosuid,nodev; the only writable path

each declared toolchain path at its host path: bind ro,nosuid,nodev; a declared path that is itself a link is created in the root as the same link (its target must be under another declared path), so paths beneath it -- .. included -- resolve as on the host; every other declared path must be canonical (no link among its parents)
/proc : only when confinement.proc; procfs subset=pid of the run's own pid namespace, nosuid,nodev,noexec (needed by rustc: glibc resolves $ORIGIN via /proc/self/exe); the host /proc is never shown
nothing else: no /etc, /home, /tmp, repository, host stage path
mechanism.final_exec: unshare --user --map-user=1000 --map-group=1000 --root=<root> --wd=/work -- <program> <args> (argv built by Atlas; chroot as uid 1000 of a nested user namespace: no capability, so no remount, no double-chroot, no new user namespace inside a chroot)
mechanism.why_chroot_not_pivot_root: after pivot_root every further step (cap drop, old-root unmount) must exist inside the new root; Atlas cannot run its own code there without unsafe code or a dependency
mechanism.probe: per run, same helper/binds/namespaces/stage: exec /work/.atlas-probe-control (0644) must answer EACCES (126); exec of the per-run host sentinel beside the stage, of the control's host path and (with proc) of /proc/1/root<sentinel> must answer ENOENT (127); each with unshare's exact `failed to execute <path>: <error>` line
mechanism.claim_rule: FILESYSTEM_CONFINED ENFORCED only when the probe passed; otherwise REFUSED CONFINEMENT_UNAVAILABLE with FILESYSTEM_CONFINED UNENFORCED{exact reason}; nothing runs unconfined in its place
mechanism.identity_rule: every run records ToolchainIdentity; identity absent -> REFUSED TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_ABSENT; pinned identity differs -> REFUSED TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH naming the first differing field, observed identity carried; chosen over a recorded mismatch because EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST admits sandbox output as evidence only with a pinned executed identity
mechanism.declarations_refused: toolchain path not absolute/normalized, missing, not dir/file, nested in another, covering /work /dev /proc, overlapping the staging directory; program not under a declared toolchain path; environment names not plain identifiers or LD_*, GCONV_PATH, GLIBC_TUNABLES, LOCPATH, NLSPATH
mechanism.both_classes: an input resolving outside the source root through a link is refused (INPUT_ESCAPES); inputs are staged as copies; a produced output that is a link or resolves outside the stage is recorded as not produced; the program is resolved once (the PATH hit or a normalized absolute path, links resolved) and the run executes that resolved file -- the one the identity digests (restricted class without a namespace: argv[0] is the found path; otherwise argv[0] is the resolved path) (review finding f1); every class executes the absolute path the program was found at (argv[0]; unshare executes the path it is given), so a multi-call binary such as the rustup proxy runs as the tool asked for, and the identity digests the file that path resolves to (they differ only by a swap between resolution and exec: RES-G189-HOST-PATH-TOCTOU); in the confined class both the found path and its target must lie under declared toolchain paths (PROGRAM_OUTSIDE_TOOLCHAIN); a program or declared binary found as or resolving to rustc must pass the name-independent sysroot rule (review round 6): `<found> --print sysroot`, run exactly as the run executes it (same class, path, declared environment, no request argument, stage still empty), exits 0 and prints an absolute sysroot whose bin/rustc canonicalizes to the resolved file; a cargo passes when the rustc beside its resolved file passes (binding the toolchain directory, not the compiler cargo invokes); otherwise TOOLCHAIN_PROXY -- a rustup proxy linked, hard-linked or copied as rustc prints the sysroot of the toolchain it selected; an earlier name-based check refuses a linked proxy before any confinement is set up (clearer message, not the soundness rule); -vV is recorded whenever the resolved file passes, whatever name it was found as, run the same way as the run; cargo -vV identifies cargo, not the compiler it invokes; declared toolchain_binaries are identified the same way and not executed by the run; the staging directory is created when missing (as at HEAD) and canonicalized, and one that cannot be created or resolved is a host error (io::Error), not a refusal
mechanism.runtime_directories: a toolchain path that is, is inside, or contains /run, /var/run, /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm (declared or resolved) is refused: a read-only bind does not stop connect() on a socket; a declared directory elsewhere that holds a socket still exposes it (RES-G189-TOOLCHAIN-SOCKETS)
mechanism.probe_environment: the probe exports the declared environment exactly as the run does (same helper argv but for the executed path); confinement_available (sandbox probe) uses an empty one
mechanism.propagation: --propagation private is passed explicitly; it is also unshare's default for --mount; this host has no shared or slave mount (0 shared:/master: in its mountinfo), so mutant N09 (unchanged) is equivalent here; the run's own mountinfo is asserted to carry no peer group

residuals.reproduction: a confined request whose program makes arbitrary system calls or forks without bound: nothing filters syscalls, nothing limits memory, CPU or pids besides the timeout
residuals.false_claim_condition: a kernel defect reachable from an unprivileged user namespace lets the program leave the chroot; the record still says FILESYSTEM_CONFINED ENFORCED (the probe ran before the program)
residuals.reopen_trigger: a seccomp or cgroup mechanism admissible without unsafe code or with a decided dependency, or a confined run used as evidence for an untrusted program

residuals.reproduction: from the host, read /proc/<outer unshare child pid>/mountinfo during a confined run: the host mount tree is present in the run's mount namespace below the chroot
residuals.false_claim_condition: the program regains CAP_SYS_CHROOT or CAP_SYS_ADMIN over the outer namespaces (kernel defect) or inherits a descriptor to a directory outside the root; it could then reach host paths while the record says ENFORCED
residuals.reopen_trigger: a pivot_root step can run inside the new root (a static helper admitted) or the mechanism changes

residuals.reproduction: declare, in a confined request, an environment variable outside LD_*, GCONV_PATH, GLIBC_TUNABLES, LOCPATH, NLSPATH that glibc acts on at process start: the pre-chroot nested unshare receives it
residuals.false_claim_condition: such a variable makes the pre-chroot unshare load or read attacker-chosen host content; reads outside the inputs happen before the chroot while the record says ENFORCED
residuals.reopen_trigger: glibc adds a start-up variable that loads code or data, or a way to apply the environment after the chroot without unsafe code

residuals.reproduction: a confined request with deny_network false: the host network and abstract unix sockets are reachable
residuals.false_claim_condition: a consumer reads FILESYSTEM_CONFINED as "cannot obtain host file content" while a host service on the network or an abstract socket serves files
residuals.reopen_trigger: a consumer (M16) relies on confinement without denying the network

residuals.reproduction: replace librustc_driver-*.so in the sysroot keeping the rustc shim and its -vV output: the pinned identity still matches
residuals.false_claim_condition: a pin is read as identifying the whole toolchain while only the program, the declared binaries and -vV are digested (the helpers unshare/sh/mount/mkdir/ln are not identified at all; cargo -vV identifies cargo, not the rustc it invokes, which RUSTC, RUSTC_WRAPPER and PATH select; a wrapper that answers --print sysroot and -vV falsely passes the sysroot rule -- it is the requester's own program, pinned by its digest, but its -vV says nothing true)
residuals.reopen_trigger: M16 hermetic build inputs, or a pin used to admit a build as evidence

residuals.reproduction: declare a toolchain directory outside /run, /var/run, /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm that holds a unix socket (or a FIFO): the read-only bind exposes it and connect() on it succeeds inside the confinement
residuals.false_claim_condition: a host service listening on a socket inside a declared directory serves host data; the run obtains it while FILESYSTEM_CONFINED says ENFORCED (reads are confined, connections are not)
residuals.reopen_trigger: a declared toolchain directory known to hold sockets, or a socket scan of declared trees becomes affordable

residuals.reproduction: id inside a confined run shows uid 1000 of the nested namespace; on the host its files are owned by the caller (root here)
residuals.false_claim_condition: none known: every visible path but /work is mounted read-only and the program has no capability; a writable host path made visible would change this
residuals.reopen_trigger: a writable path other than /work becomes visible, or an unprivileged outer uid (subordinate ids) becomes available

residuals.reproduction: run the confined tests as a non-root user on a host with unprivileged user namespaces
residuals.false_claim_condition: none: the probe gates the claim on any host; only availability is untested
residuals.reopen_trigger: Atlas runs on a non-root or non-container host

residuals.reproduction: replace a declared toolchain directory by a link to a broader directory between the declaration check and the helper bind
residuals.false_claim_condition: a concurrent host writer swaps a declared toolchain path, or a link on the program path between resolution and exec; more of the host is visible than declared (or another file runs than was identified) while the probe (which covers only the run directory and procfs) passes
residuals.reopen_trigger: toolchain paths writable by an untrusted party

residuals.reproduction: mutant M02 (exit codes only) survives the sandbox tests
